scenarioStory.history: Patient was walking to the kitchen when he suddenly felt lightheaded and collapsed to the floor, striking a chair on the way down. Witnessed by his wife, who reports he was unresponsive for approximately 15 seconds before waking on his own. He is now awake but weak, pale, and diaphoretic, with ongoing lightheadedness when attempting to sit up.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find an 82-year-old male on the kitchen floor, pale, diaphoretic, and weak following a witnessed syncopal episode. He is alert but slow to respond, with a markedly slow and irregular pulse noted on initial palpation. → Assessed and atropine given: Crew establishes IV access, applies oxygen, obtains a 12-lead confirming complete heart block, and administers atropine per protocol. As expected with third-degree block, the patient shows no significant improvement in rate or perfusion. → TCP initiated with sedation: Recognizing atropine's failure in third-degree block, the crew proceeds to transcutaneous pacing with mechanical capture confirmed, along with appropriate sedation/analgesia for patient comfort during pacing. → Capture maintained, prepared for transport: The patient remains hemodynamically stable with sustained mechanical capture on the transcutaneous pacer and adequate sedation, transported for further cardiac evaluation.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Syncopal episode, now weak and lightheaded

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find an 82-year-old male on the kitchen floor, pale, diaphoretic, and weak following a witnessed syncopal episode. He is alert but slow to respond, with a markedly slow and irregular pulse noted on initial palpation.

scenarioEvents.name: Assessed and atropine given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew establishes IV access, applies oxygen, obtains a 12-lead confirming complete heart block, and administers atropine per protocol. As expected with third-degree block, the patient shows no significant improvement in rate or perfusion.
relatedChecklist: Apply O2, initiate monitoring, obtain 12-lead EKG, establish IV access
Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a contributing cause
Atropine 1 mg IV, may repeat q3-5min (max total 3 mg)

scenarioEvents.name: TCP initiated with sedation
scenarioEvents.description: Recognizing atropine's failure in third-degree block, the crew proceeds to transcutaneous pacing with mechanical capture confirmed, along with appropriate sedation/analgesia for patient comfort during pacing.
relatedChecklist: Ketamine 21 mg IV (85 kg × 0.25 mg/kg = 21.25 mg; max initial 25 mg)
Initiate transcutaneous pacing at 70 bpm, confirm mechanical capture with palpable pulse
Ketamine 21 mg IV (85 kg × 0.25 mg/kg = 21.25 mg; max initial 25 mg) for pacing discomfort

scenarioEvents.name: Capture maintained, prepared for transport
scenarioEvents.description: The patient remains hemodynamically stable with sustained mechanical capture on the transcutaneous pacer and adequate sedation, transported for further cardiac evaluation.
relatedChecklist: Continuously reassess capture, sedation level, and vital signs en route

scenarioEvents.name: TCP performed without sedation
scenarioEvents.description: The crew initiates transcutaneous pacing but skips sedation or pain control. The patient experiences significant distress and pain from the pacing stimulus, becoming agitated and combative, which risks pad displacement and loss of capture.
relatedChecklist: Ketamine 21 mg IV (85 kg × 0.25 mg/kg = 21.25 mg; max initial 25 mg)
Ketamine 21 mg IV (85 kg × 0.25 mg/kg = 21.25 mg; max initial 25 mg) for pacing discomfort
